catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class starts, arms or resumes an instrument acquisition; cap.device.configure.v1 writes settings only and cap.sensing.read.v1 reads values.
No catalogue class forces a trigger or a one-shot acquisition; the closest classes configure settings or read values.
No catalogue class carries a single PAVA scalar measurement request/reply; cap.sensing.read.v1 returns a sensor values object, not the instrument's <parameter>,<value>,<state> reply.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: a direct Driver over oscilloscope:LeCroyScope with native.py, not the card's ScpiDriver. Every channel command is assembled at run time from a channel prefix and a command word (oscilloscope.py:368-378, 462-499), so a fixed command table cannot reproduce the wire lines and altering their syntax to fit one would be wrong. The hardware factory imports the pinned upstream module only inside connect(); the gate never imports or runs it. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (reviewed_by null), is checked on the fake backend only, and never ran hardware; this R1 package makes no hardware-review claim.

MOCK: the clone ships no simulator, mock or test suite for LeCroyScope and no instrument traffic was captured, so fake.py is an analytic in-memory stand-in, not a recording or transcript. Every fake starting value and canned reply is marked # placeholder and none is used in a Fact, Limit or the reference. The card's preferred mock strategy is transcript; it was not available.

COVERAGE: the package serves the scalar measurements and settings of the oscilloscope: identity/family/channels/bandwidth/date/acquisition status/stopped, channel-1 vdiv, offset, coupling, probe attenuation, timebase, trigger mode/source/level, writes for those settings, arm, force_trigger, a single PAVA measurement, and cap.device.calibrate.v1 around *CAL?. NOT COVERED: the waveform array (get_waveform/get_waveforms, oscilloscope.py:746-810) and the screenshot (get_screenshot, oscilloscope.py:713-744). Also not exposed: math functions, cursors, WaveSource, serial decode, bandwidth limit (BWL) and trigger delay (TRDL); the last two were dropped so the single configure tool stays within the 2048-byte MCP budget, and the channel/timebase/trigger controls above are the primary interface. The math/cursor/WaveSource/decode methods are secondary to that interface.

LIMITS: coupling, attenuation and trigger mode are closed sets stated by the vendor manual text (resources/maui_text.txt:4380, 4321 and 4619). vdiv, offset, tdiv, trigger_source and trigger_level are Limit.operator_required because the clone and the vendor text state no numeric bound (the manual refers ranges to the datasheet for vdiv/offset/tdiv, gives a Time/div-relative TRDL range, says TRLV is clamped to the nearest legal value, and says trigger sources depend on the model). site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a device fact; it fills those five paths and narrows them for one bench.

SAFETY: R1, software e-stop. The @estop calls the native stop(), which writes STOP (oscilloscope.py:577-578); the upstream has no stop acknowledgment, so the 'stopped' read (TRMD?, oscilloscope.py:580-583) is the observation that follows. The upstream 10 s VISA timeout and the shared session mean a STOP issued during an in-flight *CAL?/PAVA query may wait for that query to return or time out; the runtime latches first and does not wait for the action, but this is a software acquisition stop, not a safety-rated channel. The arm_and_wait() polling loop is intentionally not exposed because STOP does not interrupt its sleep loop. There is no @reset; a runtime reset only releases the latch, and the arm action starts a new acquisition. No reenable action is declared because STOP does not disable the device into a fault state.

G6 has one expected warning: cap.device.calibrate.v1 requires a permit, so G6 leaves its in-range call to the conformance suite; G8 ran and passed. The G8 conformance suite used the example overlay. The calibrate action accepts the class's optional standard_ref/targets/notes fields with the class length limits and descriptions, but the native *CAL? takes no reference and the driver does not send them; calibrated is true only when the *CAL? diagnostic code is 0 (resources/maui_text.txt:6081-6086).

No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings: every citation is a readable text line of the clone. check-report.json is the gate's generated report; the digest above is from the final passing run. The upstream clone was read only and is unmodified.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review checked the pinned source, every Fact and Limit, native.py, the fake and the stop path. driver.py now selects CHDR OFF before scalar reads, requires exact STOP readback, rejects failed N/A setting reads and raises on nonzero calibration diagnostics; fake.py models the reply-format setup and trigger/stop state, and test_driver.py covers the repaired failures. facts.md corrects the form-feed-sensitive manual line numbers and documents those changes; reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json were regenerated. The fake gate and strict collector pass; evidence remains contract_checked and the original RESULT.json and provenance files were preserved. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence AGPL-3.0); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Publication still requires the card owner decision (publish_review required; AGPL-3.0). STOP is acquisition-only: it does not disable WaveSource or external circuits, and the shared 10 s VISA timeout can exceed the endpoint stop budget. Another client can change COMM_HEADER or resume acquisition. The author notes retain obsolete manual line numbers and pre-fix stop/calibration descriptions; the review paragraph must explicitly supersede them. Decide the proposed direct-driver/python-object override.
